market_mood: Risk-off tone as global long-dated yields surge (UK 30-year gilts above 6%) and bank stocks slide, while oil firms on China's fuel export suspension and fresh tanker strikes in Hormuz. AI capex news keeps flowing (Broadcom's $42B Anthropic deal, Google TPUs headed to orbit) even as Micron fell despite a strong quarter.
self_check: My bearish and oil/energy calls have worked far better (75% and 78%) than my bullish AI and M&A calls, so today I leaned into rates and energy and kept tech exposure small and low-confidence.

picks.reason: UK 30-year gilt yields topped 6% for the first time since 1998 and US Treasury yields surged alongside; long-dated global bonds are in a sustained repricing that tends to unfold over days, not hours.
China suspended fuel exports and three tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz, tightening global refined product supply — a direct boost to refining margins that the market often prices in slowly.
Rising crude plus China's fuel export suspension pushes jet fuel costs higher, and commentary today flags falling earnings estimates and rising crew costs at Delta.
Wells Fargo upgraded BP to Overweight with a raised $57 target while downgrading Exxon, and firmer crude from Hormuz disruption supports the relative rotation into BP.
Wells Fargo added Microsoft to its Q4 tactical ideas list with a target far above consensus, arguing Azure and Copilot monetization is finally showing up — and tech was the only sector up this week.

watchlist_notes.note: Indexes drifting lower as Treasury yields surge; rates, not earnings, are driving the tape.
Tech is the only sector green over the week, but rising long yields are a headwind for high-multiple names.
Dow mixed, with financial weakness offsetting an Accenture-led industrial/services bounce.
No major news today; moves with the broader rate-driven tape.
Wells Fargo added Microsoft to its Q4 tactical ideas with a well-above-consensus target on Azure/Copilot monetization.
No direct news, but Broadcom's $42B Anthropic infrastructure loan and Google TPUs going to orbit highlight growing custom-silicon competition.
Anthropic's leaked S-1 chatter keeps attention on Amazon's AI investee, but no concrete company news today.
SpaceX will launch Google TPUs into orbit for space-based data centers, a long-dated validation of its chip stack.
Only executive-poaching and AI-commentary headlines; no fundamental news, and communication services was the weakest sector this week.
Coverage focuses on BYD extending its lead in Europe, a reminder of competitive pressure on Tesla's volumes.
Money-center banks sold off hard (Citi -4%, BAC -3%) as the yield surge raised funding and credit concerns.
Wells Fargo downgraded Exxon to Equal Weight on valuation while upgrading BP, a relative headwind despite firmer crude.
Gold can catch a bid from Hormuz tanker attacks and Iran escalation risk, though surging real yields cut the other way.
UK 30-year gilt yields topping 6% and surging US Treasury yields keep long-duration bond funds under pressure.

top_buys.pitch: Global long-end yields are breaking out; long bonds keep bleeding.
top_buys.why: UK 30-year gilt yields topped 6% for the first time since 1998 and US Treasury yields surged in sympathy today, hitting stocks and banks. These cross-market repricings usually grind on for days as duration holders cut exposure. TLT falls when long yields rise, so the move should keep unfolding.
top_buys.risks: A sharp risk-off panic or soft US data could send money back into Treasuries and lift TLT quickly.
top_buys.watch: Upcoming US jobs/inflation data and UK fiscal headlines driving the gilt market.

top_buys.pitch: China pulling fuel exports plus Hormuz tanker attacks tighten refined products — good for refiners.
top_buys.why: China suspending fuel exports removes a chunk of Asian diesel and gasoline supply, which typically widens refining margins globally. At the same time, three tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz and EU emergency diesel stocks are concentrated in just two countries, adding supply risk. Valero is a pure-play refiner that levers directly to wider cracks.
top_buys.risks: If China reverses the suspension or demand weakens, cracks can compress fast; refiners are volatile.
top_buys.watch: Weekly diesel crack spreads and any further Hormuz shipping incidents.

top_buys.pitch: Higher jet fuel plus rising crew costs squeeze airline margins into Q3 reports.
top_buys.why: Oil is rising on China's fuel export halt and Hormuz tanker strikes, which feeds straight into jet fuel, airlines' biggest variable cost. Commentary today highlights falling earnings estimates, rising crew costs and fuel volatility at Delta after a weak three months. Airline earnings season starts soon, giving a near-term catalyst for estimate cuts.
top_buys.risks: Oil could fade quickly, and strong premium travel demand has repeatedly bailed Delta out.
top_buys.watch: Delta's Q3 results and guidance in mid-October, and jet fuel spot prices.

top_buys.pitch: A broker upgrade plus firming crude sets up a relative rotation from Exxon into BP.
top_buys.why: Wells Fargo upgraded BP to Overweight with a $57 target while cutting Exxon to Equal Weight, calling out a valuation gap. Pair that with crude support from Hormuz disruption and China's export halt, and BP has both a catalyst and a tailwind. Upgrade-driven rotations in megacap energy often play out over weeks, not a single session.
top_buys.risks: A single broker call is thin support, and a crude pullback would hit the whole group.
top_buys.watch: Brent crude direction and BP's next quarterly update.

top_buys.pitch: Fresh Wall Street conviction that Azure and Copilot monetization is finally proving out.
top_buys.why: Wells Fargo added Microsoft to its Q4 Tactical Ideas list with a price target far above consensus, framing AI monetization as the next leg. Tech was the only sector up over the past week, so this isn't fighting the tape. Capex worries are well known, which limits the downside surprise.
top_buys.risks: Surging long yields pressure high-multiple tech, and $175B of 2026 capex could keep margins under scrutiny.
top_buys.watch: Microsoft's next quarterly report and Azure growth rate.
